lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eATP\u:
"

ATP (adenosine triphosphate) has two high-energy phosphoanhydride bonds. Its hydrolysis to ADP + Pᵢ has ΔG°′ ≈ −30.5 kJ/mol and in the cell (real concentrations) ≈ −50 kJ/mol. This is explained by the charge repulsion between phosphates, the better solvation of the products and the resonance stabilization of Pᵢ. The energy is transferred by coupling reactions.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eFAD\u:
"

FAD (from riboflavin) accepts two H at N5 and N1 of the isoalloxazine and is the coenzyme of succinate dehydrogenase and acyl-CoA dehydrogenase. Coenzyme A ends in a thiol (–SH) that forms thioesters (acetyl-CoA), with a hydrolysis ΔG°′ similar to that of ATP: “activated” acyl groups.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLas \u003cb\u003edesh:
"

Dehydrogenases take 2 e⁻ and 2 H⁺ from the substrate: NAD⁺ accepts a hydride ion (H⁻) at C4 of the nicotinamide ring, which goes from aromatic pyridinium to 1,4-dihydropyridine (NADH), and an H⁺ is released. NADH absorbs at 340 nm (NAD⁺ does not), a property used to follow enzymes. Move “Progress” to see the transfer.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eMuchos coenzimas deri:
"

Many coenzymes derive from B-complex vitamins, which humans cannot synthesize and must obtain from the diet: niacin→NAD⁺, riboflavin→FAD, pantothenic→CoA, thiamine→TPP, pyridoxine→PLP, folate→THF, biotin and B₁₂. Their deficiency affects entire pathways (beriberi, pellagra, megaloblastic anemia…).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003enucle:
"

A nucleotide consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine), a pentose (ribose or deoxyribose) and one to three phosphates. Besides being the monomers of DNA and RNA, they take part in cellular energy and signaling. The base joined to ribose by an N-glycosidic bond is a nucleoside; with phosphate, a nucleotide.

"
